title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Outline of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property in China (2016-2020)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Outline of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in China (2016-2020)"

Fa Fa [2017] No. 13

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Outline of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in China (2016-2020)" is hereby issued to you. Please implement it diligently and conscientiously.

April 20, 2017

Outline of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in China (2016-2020)

The Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation greatly stimulates mass entrepreneurship and innovation. The property rights acquired by entrepreneurs and innovators in accordance with the law shall be protected by law. Intellectual property rights, as an important type of property right, can be transformed and applied to form advanced productive forces. This is an inevitable choice for promoting supply-side structural reform in China, eliminating outdated production capacity, and enhancing international competitiveness at present and in the future. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen the judicial protection of intellectual property rights, fully realize the value of intellectual property rights, promote the creation and transformation and application of innovative achievements, and provide strong judicial guarantees for building China into a country with strong intellectual property rights and a world leader in science and technology.

China's judicial protection system for intellectual property rights started and developed amid the tide of reform and opening up. It has been continuously improved with the implementation of China's Trademark Law, Patent Law, Copyright Law, and other laws, as well as its accession to the World Trade Organization. It has gradually established a judicial protection system and mechanism for intellectual property rights, with judicial protection as the leading force, civil adjudication as the foundation, and administrative adjudication and criminal adjudication developing in parallel. This model embodies the "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese experience" in intellectual property protection, reflects the judicial rules of intellectual property rights, is an important part of China's socialist legal system, and conforms to the internationally accepted rules and practices for intellectual property protection.

I. Development Status

Over a period of more than 30 years, China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights has been constantly catching up with the path that Western developed countries have taken over nearly 300 years, forging a "Chinese path" that integrates innovation with independent development and self-improvement.

Over the past 30 years, the number of intellectual property cases in China has grown significantly. In February 1985, the people's courts accepted the first patent infringement dispute case. From 1985 to 2016, the people's courts accepted 792,851 first-instance civil intellectual property cases and concluded 766,101 cases. Administrative intellectual property cases have been separately counted since 2002. By 2016, the people's courts had accepted 44,401 first-instance administrative intellectual property cases and concluded 39,113 cases. Criminal intellectual property cases have been separately counted since 1998. By 2016, the people's courts had accepted 77,116 first-instance criminal intellectual property cases and concluded 76,174 cases. The scope of intellectual property protection covers all types of intellectual property rights stipulated in the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) as well as acts of unfair competition. Judicial protection of intellectual property rights in areas such as China's time-honored brands, traditional Chinese medicine, Chinese folk literature and art, and Chinese font libraries has brought vibrant vitality to the ancient Chinese civilization.

Over the past 30 years, the trial mechanism for intellectual property cases in China has gradually improved. In October 1995, the Intellectual Property Division of the Supreme People's Court was established. In November 2014, the Beijing, Guangzhou, and Shanghai Intellectual Property Courts were established successively. In early 2017, specialized intellectual property adjudication bodies in Nanjing, Suzhou, Chengdu, and Wuhan were established. In July 2016, the "three-in-one" trial model for civil, administrative, and criminal intellectual property cases was implemented nationwide. A diversified mechanism for ascertaining technical facts, involving technical investigation officers, judicial appraisals, expert assistants, and expert consultations, has been preliminarily formed. The jurisdictional structure, under which the Beijing Intellectual Property Court has jurisdiction over patent and trademark administrative cases concerning grant and confirmation of rights according to law, some intermediate people's courts have centralized jurisdiction over technical civil cases such as patent cases, and some basic people's courts have jurisdiction over general intellectual property cases, has become more reasonable. As of the end of 2016, there were 224 intermediate people's courts designated by the Supreme People's Court or enjoying special jurisdiction according to law over civil disputes involving patents, new plant varieties, integrated circuit layout designs, monopolies, and the recognition of well-known trademarks. In addition, the Supreme People's Court also approved 167 basic people's courts to have jurisdiction over general civil intellectual property cases.

Over the past 30 years, China's judicial policies on intellectual property rights have been continuously improved. The Supreme People's Court guides trial practice by formulating judicial policies, ensuring the uniform and transparent application of legal standards for resolving disputes concerning the creation, use, and transaction of intellectual property rights in different periods, regions, and fields, which is practical and effective; and ensuring the organic unity of upholding the Party's leadership, ensuring the people's position as masters of the country, and governing the country according to law in intellectual property trial work. From 1985 to 2016, a total of 34 judicial interpretations and more than 40 judicial policy documents concerning intellectual property rights were formulated, effectively playing the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights. Especially since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Supreme People's Court has firmly implemented the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's series of important speeches and the new concepts, ideas, and strategies for governing the country, increased the intensity of judicial reform, continuously broken down institutional and mechanistic obstacles restricting intellectual property protection, and proposed the basic policy for judicial protection of intellectual property rights, which is "judicial leadership, strict protection, differentiated measures, and proportional coordination" for the present and future periods.

The practice and experience of the past 30 years have proven that judicial protection of intellectual property rights is crucial to the implementation of the innovation-driven development strategy, to the prosperity of economic, social, and cultural development, to both domestic and international situations, and is receiving increasing attention from all sectors of society and the international community. To this end, the Supreme People's Court has established the "Supreme People's Court Research Center for Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights," the "Supreme People's Court (Beijing) Base for Research on Guiding Cases on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights," the "China Court (Shanghai) Base for International Exchange on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights," and the "Supreme People's Court (Guangdong) Base for Research on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights and Market Value." It regularly publishes the "Report on the Status of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in Chinese Courts," the "Annual Report on Intellectual Property Cases of the Supreme People's Court," and the "Yearbook of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in China," timely summarizing and authoritatively presenting new achievements and experiences in China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights, striving to ensure that the people feel fairness and justice in every judicial case.

The practice and experience of the past 30 years have proven that judicial protection of intellectual property rights must be based on the basic national condition that China is still in the primary stage of socialist development, closely focus on the goal of modernizing the national governance system and governance capacity, adhere to an open mindset, maintain a global perspective, strictly abide by international conventions, actively participate in international governance practices concerning intellectual property rights, promptly voice China's opinions, and fully demonstrate the international influence of China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights.

The practice and experience of the past 30 years have proven that to give full play to the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights, it is necessary to build an adjudication team that administers justice for the people and exercises impartial justice, always adhering to firm beliefs, professional competence, excellent conduct, integrity and self-discipline, innovative spirit, and a sense of responsibility. Currently, there are over 5,000 intellectual property judges, judge assistants, technical investigation officers, and court clerks in courts nationwide. They inherit the advanced concepts of judicial protection of intellectual property rights and promote the development and progress of China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights, forming a team that the Party and the people can rely on.

Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the new economic development concepts of "innovation, coordination, green development, openness, and sharing" have placed higher demands on the judicial protection of intellectual property rights. At the same time, the world is ushering in a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation. Developed countries have taken intellectual property rights as a powerful weapon to seize the commanding heights of the global economy and technology, implementing high-standard intellectual property protection rules in international trade. Intellectual property rights have increasingly become a core element of international competitiveness. Facing the new domestic and international situation, in accordance with the "Outline of the Thirteenth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development of the People's Republic of China," the "Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Improving the Property Rights Protection System and Legally Protecting Property Rights," the "Several Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Deepening Institutional Reforms and Mechanisms to Accelerate the Implementation of the Innovation-Driven Development Strategy," and the "Outline of the National Intellectual Property Strategy," and other decisions and deployments, combined with the actual work of judicial protection of intellectual property rights in the people's courts, this "Outline of Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights in China (2016-2020)" is hereby formulated. Through five years of effort, we strive to further improve the judicial protection system for intellectual property rights, enhance judicial protection capabilities, further highlight the leading role of judicial protection, and provide more "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese experience" for international judicial protection of intellectual property rights.

II. Guiding Ideology

Adhere to the guidance of Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the important thought of the "Three Represents," and the Scientific Outlook on Development; fully implement the spirit of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Third, Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee; deeply implement the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's series of important speeches and the new concepts, ideas, and strategies for governing the country; firmly establish the "Four Consciousnesses"; in accordance with the requirements of the "Five-in-One" overall layout and the "Four Comprehensives" strategic layout, closely focus on the goal of "striving to ensure that the people feel fairness and justice in every judicial case"; adhere to administering justice for the people and exercising impartial justice; continuously deepen judicial reform; give full play to the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights; establish the concept that protecting intellectual property rights means protecting innovation; provide effective judicial services for implementing the national intellectual property strategy and the innovation-driven development strategy; and provide strong judicial guarantees for achieving the "Two Centenary Goals" and building China into a country with strong intellectual property rights and a world leader in science and technology.

III. Basic Principles

(1) Adhere to serving the overall situation. Serving the overall situation is the fundamental mission of the trial work of the people's courts and an important duty of intellectual property adjudication. It is necessary to effectively enhance the awareness of the overall situation, strengthen the sense of historical mission and responsibility, closely focus on the overall situation of the Party and the country's development, actively adapt to new changes in the international situation, and identify the focal points of intellectual property trial work.

(2) Adhere to reform and innovation. Reform and innovation are the dynamic source for the sustained and healthy development of intellectual property adjudication and the only way to modernize the trial system and trial capacity. For key areas and weak links that affect and restrict the development of intellectual property adjudication, it is necessary to use innovative concepts and methods to solve problems, make up for shortcomings, continuously improve the trial system and mechanism, and accelerate the modernization of the judicial system and judicial capacity for intellectual property rights.

(3) Adhere to judicial leadership. Giving play to the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights is an inherent requirement of the essential attributes of the judiciary and the laws of intellectual property protection, and an important manifestation of comprehensively advancing the rule of law. It is necessary to strengthen the concept of judicial leadership, give full play to the institutional and mechanistic advantages of judicial protection, properly handle the relationship between judicial protection and administrative protection, strengthen the procedural review of administrative law enforcement actions and the substantive review of enforcement standards, strengthen supervision while legally supporting administrative law enforcement actions, and enforce strict regulation.

(4) Adhere to equal protection. The legitimate rights and interests of intellectual property rights of economic entities under different ownership systems and parties of different nationalities shall be equally protected. It is necessary to adhere to equal rights, equal opportunities, and equal rules. Whether it is the public economy or the non-public economy, whether it is domestic parties or foreign parties, the parties must be effectively guaranteed to enjoy equal procedural and substantive rights in intellectual property litigation.

(5) Adhere to strict protection. Strict protection of intellectual property rights is an inevitable requirement for implementing the innovation-driven development strategy and is the basic direction of China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights at present and in the future. It is necessary to take fully realizing the value of intellectual property rights as the guide, take being conducive to stimulating innovation as the starting point, strictly implement the law, and effectively improve the pertinence and effectiveness of judicial protection of intellectual property rights.

(6) Adhere to differentiated measures. Correctly grasp the protection needs and characteristics of different types of intellectual property rights, such as technological achievements and business identifiers; properly define the judgment standards for unfair competition and monopoly acts; continuously strengthen research and solutions for key links, special areas, and specific issues; adopt differentiated measures according to the different types and fields of intellectual property rights, so that the protection methods, means, and standards are compatible with the characteristics and needs of the intellectual property rights.

(7) Adhere to proportional coordination. Balance protecting rights and stimulating innovation; insist that the scope and intensity of intellectual property protection are coordinated with the degree of innovation and contribution; the cost of infringement to the infringer is commensurate with the degree of subjective malice and the harmfulness of the act; intellectual property protection is compatible with the laws of development, national conditions, actual needs, and development; reasonably balance the interests of the right holder, the legitimate interests of others, the public interest, and the national interest according to law; and achieve the harmonious unity of protecting intellectual property rights and promoting technological innovation and industrial development.

(8) Adhere to open development. Enhancing the international influence of China's judicial protection of intellectual property rights is an inevitable requirement for building China into a country with strong intellectual property rights that is Chinese-characteristic and world-class. It is necessary to adhere to an international perspective and a global vision, base on reality and national conditions, respect international rules and mainstream practices, boldly absorb and draw lessons from international experience in judicial protection of intellectual property rights, carefully summarize and actively promote Chinese experience in judicial protection of intellectual property rights, and continuously enhance China's leading role in international governance rules for intellectual property.

IV. Main Objectives

(1) Establish a coordinated and open policy system for judicial protection of intellectual property rights. Establish a coordinated and open judicial policy system that governs the application of legal standards, adjudication reasoning, and the value orientation of judgments.

(2) Establish a clear and unified system of rules for judgment standards on intellectual property rights. Establish a clear and unified system of rules for determining the scope of rights, identifying infringing acts, calculating damages, and accepting the validity of evidence.

(3) Establish a balanced system of intellectual property courts. Establish a system of intellectual property courts with balanced development in regional layout, horizontal relationships, vertical relationships, and the "three-in-one" mechanism.

(4) Establish a rationally structured system of jurisdiction rules for intellectual property cases. Establish a system of rules for territorial jurisdiction, hierarchical jurisdiction, exclusive jurisdiction, and cross-regional centralized jurisdiction.

(5) Establish a system of evidence rules suitable for the characteristics of intellectual property cases. Establish a coordinated system of evidence rules that integrates the provision of evidence by the parties, the court's ex officio investigation and collection of evidence and evidence preservation, and the disclosure of evidence and exclusion of evidence obstruction.

(6) Establish a scientific and reasonable system for calculating damages in intellectual property cases. Establish a system for calculating damages that adapts the losses suffered by the right holder due to infringement, the profits gained by the infringer, license fees, statutory damages, and litigation costs to the value of the intellectual property rights.

(7) Build a high-quality team of intellectual property judges. Build a team of intellectual property judges who exercise impartial justice, administer justice for the people, can hear civil, administrative, and criminal intellectual property cases with high quality and efficiency, and possess an international perspective.

(8) Establish a long-term mechanism for international judicial exchange and cooperation on intellectual property rights. Actively promote the implementation of China's "Belt and Road" and "Going Global" strategies and the "Made in China 2025" strategy, and create an international environment of fairness, justice, and orderly competition.

V. Key Measures

(1) Fairly and Efficiently Adjudicate Various Types of Intellectual Property Cases

Actively improve the trial mechanism for cases involving overlapping civil and administrative proceedings, avoid circular litigation, and accelerate the substantive resolution of disputes. Promote the simplification of procedures for simple cases and the meticulous handling of complex cases. Implement differentiated handling of trial procedures and judgment documents based on different trial levels and case types, achieving quick adjudication of simple cases and refined adjudication of complex cases. Appropriately expand the scope of application of summary procedures; for simple intellectual property cases where the facts are clear, rights and obligations are clear, and disputes are minor, the trial procedures may be simplified. Give full play to the role of the judicial committee in summarizing trial experience and strengthening trial guidance to improve trial quality and efficiency.

(2) Establish Effective Mechanisms to Ensure the Correct Implementation of Laws

Carefully summarize the issues concerning the application of law in administrative dispute cases concerning patent and trademark grant and confirmation, trademark civil dispute cases, and pre-litigation interim injunctions; formulate relevant judicial interpretations in a timely manner to unify judgment standards and criteria. Promote the revision of judicial interpretations on new plant varieties and strengthen the judicial protection of new plant variety rights. Actively conduct research on cutting-edge issues concerning the application of law, including standard-essential patents, new business models, collective management of copyright, and the protection of intellectual property rights in the information network environment. Strengthen research on the protection of intellectual property rights related to traditional Chinese medicine, folk literature and art, and intangible cultural heritage; formulate judicial policies in a timely manner and clarify judgment principles and requirements. Strengthen research on intellectual property disputes arising in the construction of free trade zones, such as parallel imports, transit and transshipment, and original equipment manufacturing (OEM) processing, and properly resolve them. Actively participate in the revision of laws such as the Patent Law, Copyright Law, and Anti-Unfair Competition Law; strive to elevate relevant rules from judicial interpretations and judicial policies into law; and promote the resolution of problems existing in the actual operation of the "dual-track system" of judicial protection and administrative protection of intellectual property rights.

(3) Comprehensively Promote the "Three-in-One" Trial Model for Civil, Administrative, and Criminal Intellectual Property Cases

Following the judicial rules of intellectual property rights, construct a centralized, three-dimensional trial model that is "three-level linkage, three-judgment integration, and tripartite integration" in line with actual conditions, focusing on solving issues of coordination and cooperation in the investigation, arrest, public prosecution, and trial stages of criminal intellectual property cases. The High People's Courts shall establish communication and liaison mechanisms between the people's courts within their jurisdiction and the procuratorial organs, public security organs, and administrative law enforcement organs for intellectual property rights, coordinating with the public security and procuratorial organs for the investigation, transfer, and prosecution of criminal cases. The High and Intermediate People's Courts shall establish corresponding coordination organizations responsible for guiding and supervising the "three-in-one" work within their jurisdictions. Appropriately allocate trial personnel according to work needs, increase training efforts, and strive to build a team of compound judges capable of handling the three types of litigation (civil, administrative, criminal). Intellectual property courts shall promptly carry out the "three-in-one" trial in accordance with relevant decisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

(4) Continuously Improve the Jurisdiction System for Intellectual Property Cases

In accordance with the principles of appropriate concentration, reasonable layout, and the "three-in-one" trial model for intellectual property cases, coordinate and determine the territorial, hierarchical, and specialized jurisdiction of intellectual property cases. Within the jurisdiction of an Intermediate People's Court, general civil, administrative, and criminal intellectual property cases shall, in principle, be assigned to one designated Basic People's Court with cross-regional centralized jurisdiction. In areas with a high volume of cases, the number of designated Basic People's Courts with jurisdiction may be appropriately increased. In areas with a low volume of cases, the Intermediate People's Court may exercise jurisdiction at the first instance (elevated jurisdiction). Hierarchical jurisdiction shall be determined primarily based on the type of case, gradually achieving centralized jurisdiction over technical cases. The conditions, scope, and procedures for the transfer of case jurisdiction shall be clarified. Major, difficult, complex, or socially significant cases may be subject to elevated jurisdiction by a higher people's court. Intellectual property courts and tribunals shall exercise cross-administrative-region specialized jurisdiction over civil, administrative, and criminal cases involving technical matters such as patents.

(5) Formulate Evidence Rules for Intellectual Property Litigation in a Timely Manner

(6) Continuously Improve Mechanisms for Ascertaining Technical Facts

Clarify the methods by which technical investigation officers, technical consulting experts, and technical appraisal personnel participate in the investigation of technical facts. Fully utilize various resources and forces for technical investigation to construct an organically coordinated technical fact investigation and determination system, thereby enhancing the scientific, professional, and neutral nature of technical fact ascertainment. Standardize the writing format and adoption mechanism of technical investigation reports. For technical investigation opinions that assist judges in forming inner conviction and have significant relevance to the adjudication result, limited disclosure may be made to the parties through explanatory means. Strengthen the leading role of judges in ascertaining technical facts, and standardize the legal positioning of various technical review opinions provided by technical investigation subjects.

(7) Establish an Infringement Compensation System Oriented Towards Full Realization of the Value of Intellectual Property

Vigorously promote the concept of respecting knowledge and talent. Adhere to the value orientation that the creation of intellectual property generates value, that right holders are entitled to returns on their interests, and that infringement of intellectual property constitutes infringement on both personal and property rights of others. Establish a fair, reasonable, proportionate, and coordinated compensation system for intellectual property damages, with compensatory damages as the primary measure and punitive damages as supplementary, ensuring that the interests of right holders are compensated, that infringers derive no profit, and that the losing party bears the costs of rights enforcement. Promote the inclusion of punitive damages provisions in laws such as the Copyright Law, the Patent Law, and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and increase the statutory amount of compensation for intellectual property infringement. In accordance with the decision-making requirements of the "Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Deepening Institutional and Mechanism Reforms to Accelerate the Implementation of the Innovation-Driven Development Strategy" and the "Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Improving the Property Rights Protection System and Legally Protecting Property Rights," achieve a historic shift towards strict protection of intellectual property.

(8) Study Issues Concerning Special Procedural Law for Intellectual Property Litigation

To meet the needs of the "three-in-one" (civil, administrative, criminal) intellectual property trial mode, actively carry out special research on special procedural law for intellectual property litigation, and at an appropriate time, take appropriate measures to promote the formulation of a special procedural law that conforms to the characteristics of intellectual property trials. Through the special procedural law, establish the rules on territorial jurisdiction, subject-matter jurisdiction, and exclusive jurisdiction for intellectual property civil, administrative, and criminal cases, as well as the rules of evidence and evidence preservation in intellectual property litigation. Further clarify the function of the people's court in civil patent and trademark litigation to review the validity of patents and registered trademarks, and clarify the litigation rights, obligations, and responsibilities of technical investigation officers, expert assistants, and technical consulting experts.

(9) Promote the Improvement of Specialized Intellectual Property Trial Institutions

Actively implement the spirit of the "Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Coordinated Development Outline." The Supreme People's Court is responsible for overall coordination of cross-regional jurisdiction over technology-related cases in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. Explore the establishment of branch tribunals by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court in Tianjin Municipality and Hebei Province to centrally hear technology-related cases in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, and on this basis, promote other intellectual property courts to centrally hear technology-related cases across a larger scope across administrative regions. Conscientiously summarize the work and experience since the establishment of specialized intellectual property trial institutions in Chongqing, Nanjing, Suzhou, Wuhan, and Chengdu. Based on the actual needs of trial work, appropriately establish additional intellectual property courts in accordance with the law, and improve the rational layout of specialized intellectual property trial institutions.

(10) Study and Construct an Appeal Mechanism for Intellectual Property Cases

In accordance with the requirement of "exploring the establishment of an intellectual property appellate court" set forth in the 2008 "National Intellectual Property Strategy Outline," conduct in-depth research on establishing an appeal mechanism for intellectual property cases at the national level, from the perspective of the country's long-term development strategy and with a broad vision adapting to international development trends. Strive to resolve, at the institutional level, the problem of inconsistent legal application standards in final judgments nationwide due to the decentralized jurisdiction of second-instance trials of technology-related cases, which affects judicial credibility.

(11) Actively Promote the Intellectual Property Case Guidance System

The guiding cases on intellectual property published by the Supreme People's Court, cases in the Gazette, typical cases published by the Intellectual Property Tribunal of the Supreme People's Court, cases published by the "Beijing Base for Intellectual Property Case Guidance Research (Supreme People's Court)," and typical intellectual property cases published by the Judicial Case Research Institute of the Supreme People's Court shall form a scientific and reasonable case cluster, clarifying the selection mechanism, validity hierarchy, publishing body, and publishing method for each type of case. Construct a system where guiding cases and reference cases coexist, achieving a dynamic interaction mechanism where various cases are strictly and normatively generated and continuously codified, updated, and replaced. Establish a nationwide database of intellectual property cases, and create an intelligent case information management and application system.

(12) Promote the Establishment of a Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism for Intellectual Property

Effectively leverage the positive role of arbitration and other dispute resolution methods in resolving intellectual property disputes, and encourage parties to resolve disputes through non-litigation means. Strengthen communication with arbitration institutions, industry associations, and mediation organizations, promote the construction of third-party platforms for the resolution of intellectual property civil disputes, and smooth the connection mechanism between litigation, arbitration, and mediation, unifying relevant procedures and legal documents. Support arbitration institutions and mediation organizations in lawfully performing their duties in aspects such as evidence preservation, property preservation, and enforcement, forming a convenient mechanism for non-litigation resolution of intellectual property disputes.

(13) Comprehensively Promote Judicial Transparency in Intellectual Property

Actively explore new avenues for judicial transparency in the mobile internet environment, strengthen the extensive application of intellectual property trials to platforms such as China Judgments Online, China Trial Process Information Online, and China Court Hearings Online, and promote the informatization, datamation, and refinement of judicial transparency in intellectual property. Strengthen the construction of technology courts, use video, audio, and other technologies to make trial processes public, vigorously promote simultaneous audio and video recording of court sessions and live webcasting of trials, innovate forms of trial transparency, and expand the scope of trial transparency. Introduce third-party professional institutions such as data analysis agencies and new internet media to analyze and research judicial data, strengthen the application of results of judicial transparency, and enhance the intelligence of judicial transparency. Properly carry out the drafting and publication of the "White Paper on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property in Chinese Courts," the "Annual Report on Intellectual Property Cases of the Supreme People's Court," and the "Ten Major Cases and Fifty Typical Cases," among others.

(14) Continue to Strengthen International Exchange and Cooperation

Relying on the "Shanghai Base for International Exchange on Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property of Chinese Courts," build an internationally oriented intellectual property think tank, actively carry out intellectual property seminars and exchange activities with international influence, and publicize China's achievements in judicial protection of intellectual property. Further expand the space for international exchanges and cooperation. By sending personnel to participate in international conferences, overseas training, organizing international forums, and inviting foreign judges and scholars to China for exchanges, promptly understand and grasp international trends in intellectual property protection, and promote mutual communication and cooperation. Through various dialogue platforms, actively participate in and guide the creation and revision of international intellectual property governance rules, promoting the construction of a more fair, just, open, and transparent set of international rules.

(15) Build a High-Quality Intellectual Property Trial Team

Strengthen ideological and political construction, improve judicial work style, and ensure judicial integrity. Through various methods such as temporary assignments and permanent appointments, establish diverse personnel exchange systems among intellectual property courts, specialized intellectual property trial institutions, and higher and lower courts, gradually achieving the integration of the construction of intellectual property judge teams nationwide. Focus on cultivating a group of intellectual property judges who have a global perspective, are proficient in law, understand technology, and possess an international vision. Promote categorized personnel management, clarifying the responsibilities and management requirements for judges, judge assistants, technical investigation officers, and court clerks. Standardize the selection conditions, types of appointments, recusal systems, and training mechanisms for technical investigation officers.

The Supreme People's Court shall be responsible for the specific organization and implementation of this Outline, establishing corresponding coordination and guidance bodies as needed, and determining the timetable and roadmap for the implementation of each key measure in this Outline. Establish a system for reporting the situation, promptly summarize experiences, strengthen supervision and guidance, and promote local people's courts at all levels to complete various work tasks on schedule. People's courts at all levels shall actively carry out public opinion and publicity work, creating a favorable external environment for the judicial protection of intellectual property.
